title: Body size and the architecture of the visual system in crepuscular and diurnal bees
journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
why: Peponapis, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: the stored abstract says the authors measured the sizes of the ocellus, compound eyes, ommatidial density and dorsal, frontal and ventral facets of 11 phylogenetically related bee species with different temporal patterns. title: Behavioral spectral sensitivity in the hummingbird: a peak in the UV
why: Eupetomena, lambda_max_nm and spectral_range_nm: a University of São Paulo repository record that both "Eupetomena spectral sensitivity" and "swallow-tailed hummingbird spectral sensitivity" returned as their first result; its title reports a behavioural spectral sensitivity with an ultraviolet peak in "the hummingbird". The same repository holds the 1998 ARVO abstract of Takase, de Souza and Ventura on the oil droplets of Eupetomena macroura (main logs it, sweep-55#5), so the 1997 record probably concerns the same species and may give a behavioural peak (main files such peaks under lambda_max_nm, as for the dog and the slider turtle) and the range of wavelengths the bird responds to; that it is a meeting abstract, like the 1998 record, is my inference. Title, year and link from the search result; not opened. Authors are left blank because the search result does not show them.

title: Eye morphology and retinal topography in hummingbirds (Trochilidae: Aves)
why: Eupetomena, acuity_cpd and interreceptor_deg: a study of eye morphology and retinal ganglion cell topography in hummingbirds by Lisney and colleagues of the Iwaniuk laboratory; main's wanted line for it (sweep-55) targets this species, and audit 63 found that three of its five species are named in pages it opened (Amazilia tzacatl, Calypte anna and Phaethornis superciliosus), so whether the swallow-tailed hummingbird is one of the other two is unseen. A ganglion-cell map gives an anatomical acuity and a cell spacing. Title and link from the search result "Lisney eye morphology and retinal topography in hummingbirds Trochilidae"; year, DOI and authors are left blank because the result shows them only on pages not opened.
